sources: Jegham et al. (2025), arXiv:2505.09598 (v6, Nov 2025) — provider PUE/WUE/CIF methodology
Microsoft Environmental Sustainability Report FY2024 (Azure PUE 1.12, fleet WUE 0.30 L/kWh)
AWS Sustainability Report 2024 (PUE 1.15, global WUE 0.15 L/kWh)
Google, Measuring the environmental impact of delivering AI at Google (arXiv:2508.15734, Aug 2025) — fleet PUE 1.09, consumptive WUE 1.15 L/kWh (ISO Cat 2)
Mytton (2021), Data centre water consumption, npj Clean Water — US electricity-generation water intensity ~2.18 L/kWh (off-site WUE)
IEA Electricity 2025 — global grid 445 gCO2/kWh (2024); Ember US Electricity 2025 — US 384 gCO2/kWh (2024)
ScienceDirect 2025 (US ISO 2024 averages): CAISO ~230, ERCOT ~371, PJM ~398 gCO2e/kWh
_metadata.notes: wue_offsite is the water consumed by electricity GENERATION for the grid supplying the data center (this off-site water often exceeds on-site cooling — we include BOTH, unlike most provider disclosures); cif values are location-based unless noted.

lifecycle.notes: Multiplier on operational carbon to amortize hardware manufacturing and data-center construction, following the lifecycle boundary used by Google's 2025 per-prompt analysis and Mistral AI's 2025 LCA. Set includeEmbodied=false in the engine to disable.

google_cloud.name: Google Cloud
google_cloud.notes: Hosts Gemini models; industry-lowest fleet PUE. WUE is Google's own ISO Cat 2 consumptive figure (used in their Gemini per-prompt paper). CIF is location-based; Google's market-based figure is far lower due to clean-energy purchasing.

mistral_eu.name: Mistral (EU, France-dominant)
mistral_eu.notes: French grid is nuclear-dominant — very low carbon intensity

xai.name: xAI (Memphis, TN)
xai.notes: Estimated — site partially powered by on-site gas turbines, raising effective carbon intensity
xai.source: Estimate from public reporting on the Memphis site (2025)
